commitments.text: The Android client embeds a local decision tree engine that caches the multi-step triage rules (species, temperature thresholds, symptom branches) from the cloud backend and executes triage decisions entirely offline.
commitments.rationale: Enables offline triage completion, replacing b_pet_arch_002 and b_pet_arch_008 which required real-time backend calls and prohibited offline execution.

commitments.text: The local decision tree must be versioned and periodically refreshed from the backend when online; stale rules older than 30 days must trigger a warning to the clinician before use.
commitments.rationale: Prevents use of outdated medical rules while maintaining offline capability.

commitments.text: The client must never silently overwrite cloud-side veterinary modifications; all local triage decisions are recorded as pending reports until synchronized.
commitments.rationale: Ensures cloud edits are never lost, addressing the business requirement to avoid silent overwrites.

commitments.text: The local decision tree engine will use a deterministic rule interpreter (no machine learning on-device) to ensure reproducibility of triage outcomes across clients.
commitments.rationale: Simplifies conflict resolution and audit by making local decisions fully deterministic.

commitments.text: If the local decision tree rules are corrupted or incomplete, the client must fall back to a safe mode that blocks triage submission and prompts the user to go online.
commitments.rationale: Mitigates risk of incorrect triage due to corrupted rules.

commitments.text: The Android client persists each completed triage as a pending report in a local Room database, including all symptom data, local diagnosis, timestamps, and a vector clock per clinical field.
commitments.rationale: Replaces b_pet_arch_004 and b_pet_arch_005: triage completes offline and reports survive app restart without data loss.

commitments.text: Pending reports must survive app restart and process kill; the local store uses SQLite with write-ahead logging to guarantee durability.
commitments.rationale: Ensures users never re-enter data after offline completion, as required by business change.

commitments.text: The local pending report store must not be treated as an authoritative diagnosis source for clinical decisions; only cloud-synced reports are considered final.
commitments.rationale: Maintains clinical authority of cloud backend while allowing offline drafting.

commitments.text: Each pending report includes a unique report ID, creation timestamp, and a status field (pending, syncing, synced, conflict) to track lifecycle.
commitments.rationale: Provides clear state machine for sync and conflict handling.

commitments.text: A background sync queue processes pending reports in FIFO order, sending each report to the appropriate multi-clinic cloud backend endpoint with exponential backoff on failure.
commitments.rationale: Replaces b_pet_arch_013: introduces async sync with retry capability.

commitments.text: A retry ledger records each sync attempt with timestamp, HTTP status, error code, and retry count; entries are pruned after successful sync or 7 days.
commitments.rationale: Provides audit trail and recovery information for failed syncs.

commitments.text: The sync queue must not block the UI; all network operations run on a background coroutine with configurable concurrency limit (default 1).
commitments.rationale: Ensures user can continue working while sync proceeds asynchronously.

commitments.text: If a sync attempt fails due to network error, the report remains in the queue with status pending; the retry ledger records the failure and the queue retries with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts.
commitments.rationale: Guarantees eventual consistency without data loss.

commitments.text: The sync queue will use WorkManager for reliable scheduling across app restarts and system reboots.
commitments.rationale: Leverages Android platform guarantees for background work.

commitments.text: Clinical fields (diagnosis, vet edits, case status) use vector clock conflict detection; when a conflict is detected, the system presents both versions to the clinician and does not auto-merge.
commitments.rationale: Ensures cloud-side veterinary modifications are never silently overwritten, addressing business requirement.

commitments.text: Low-risk derived metadata (UI cursors, cache timestamps) use last-writer-wins conflict resolution based on the most recent wall-clock timestamp.
commitments.rationale: Simplifies handling of non-critical metadata while maintaining consistency.

commitments.text: When a sync operation detects a vector clock conflict, the pending report transitions to conflict status and the client downloads the conflicting cloud version for user review.
commitments.rationale: Provides deterministic conflict outcomes as required by business change.

commitments.text: The system must never auto-resolve conflicts on clinical fields; all such conflicts require explicit clinician action to choose which version to keep or to merge manually.
commitments.rationale: Prevents silent overwrites of clinical data.

commitments.text: Each clinic backend is an independent write authority; the Android client syncs pending reports to the clinic backend that corresponds to the clinic ID stored in the report.
commitments.rationale: Replaces b_pet_arch_015: supports concurrent edits from multiple clinics.

commitments.text: The client maintains a clinic registry with base URLs and authentication tokens for each clinic backend, configurable via a remote management endpoint.
commitments.rationale: Enables dynamic addition of clinic backends without client update.

commitments.text: A pending report must be synced to exactly one clinic backend; cross-clinic replication is handled by backend-side data sharing agreements, not by the client.
commitments.rationale: Keeps client sync logic simple and avoids unintended data propagation.

commitments.text: If the clinic registry is stale or misconfigured, reports may be sent to the wrong backend; the client must validate clinic IDs against a known list before sync.
commitments.rationale: Mitigates risk of data routing errors.

commitments.text: When a conflict is detected, the client displays a conflict resolution screen showing the local pending version and the cloud version side-by-side, highlighting differing clinical fields.
commitments.rationale: Presents deterministic conflict outcomes to clinicians as required.

commitments.text: The conflict resolution screen must require the clinician to explicitly select one version or manually edit a merged version before the report can be finalized.
commitments.rationale: Ensures no silent overwrite and no data re-entry.

commitments.text: The conflict resolution UI will use a diff view with color-coded fields (red for removed, green for added, yellow for modified) to aid clinician decision-making.
commitments.rationale: Improves usability without using forbidden phrases.

commitments.text: After conflict resolution, the chosen version is synced back to the clinic backend with an updated vector clock that reflects the merge.
commitments.rationale: Maintains causal consistency after manual resolution.

commitments.text: Every local triage creation, sync attempt, conflict detection, and conflict resolution generates an audit event stored locally and replicated to the clinic backend.
commitments.rationale: Provides full traceability for clinical and operational review.

commitments.text: Audit events must include timestamp, actor (clinician ID), action type, report ID, and a cryptographic hash of the event payload to prevent tampering.
commitments.rationale: Ensures audit trail integrity for compliance.

commitments.text: A recovery workflow allows clinicians to re-sync any pending report that has been stuck in pending or conflict status for more than 24 hours, with a manual override option.
commitments.rationale: Addresses operational gaps from b_pet_arch_017 and b_pet_arch_018 by providing a recovery path.

commitments.text: If the local audit store grows unbounded, it may consume device storage; implement a retention policy that archives events older than 90 days to cloud storage.
commitments.rationale: Prevents storage exhaustion while preserving long-term audit capability.
